newsitem.title: USA: Illinois judge reverses ruling in park dist. case.
newsitem.headline: Illinois judge reverses ruling in park dist. case.

text.p: Park districts in DuPage County, Ill., breathed a sigh of relief Tuesday when a circuit court judge ruled that the application of an Illinois property tax limitation law to certain park district debt would violate the state and U.S. Constitution.

Judge John Darrah reversed his April 1996 ruling that property taxes used by the Lisle Park District to pay off general obligation debt issued for the retirement of about $6 million of installment contracts and alternate bonds were subject to limitations under a 1991 state tax cap law.
That ruling led park districts in DuPage County to warn of pending financial doom.

Lawyers representing the county tax collector in the case brought by business taxpayers in the county then argued that Darrah's April ruling would unconstitutionally impair the park district's contracts with bondholders.
Because the lawsuit against Lisle Park District was termed a test case it stood to affect several other park districts in the county.

Tuesday, Darrah ruled that the application of the tax cap law would violate the contract clauses of the Illinois constitution and U.S. Constitution because it would impair park district contracts with bondholders.
Susan Crowley, a Chicago attorney representing the business taxpayers, said Darrah's new ruling would be appealed to the Illinois Appellate Court.
